java: TContext#buildCodeIterator wraps the TIM body with CodeIteratorLongComment, CodeIteratorShortComment, and CodeIteratorInnerComment before plain lines are added to the result stream later hashed by UmlSource#seed.
TLineType marks full-line quote comments and whole-line /' ... '/ comments as COMMENT_SIMPLE; it marks long comments only when a /' line has no closing '/ token.
CodeIteratorLongComment consumes COMMENT_LONG_START through the line whose trimmed text ends with '/.

StringLocated#removeInnerComment preserves code after a prefix /' ... '/ inner comment, preserves code before a suffix /' ... '/ inner comment, and removes only /'''[-\w]*'''/ payloads for triple inner comments.
No Java source path inspected supports the broad claim that every ordinary trailing apostrophe comment is removed before UmlSource#seed; the shipped behavior is command/parser dependent.
rust: expanded_theme_seed_source reconstructs theme-expanded source and sends non-theme user lines through post_tim_seed_line.
post_tim_seed_line drops any line whose trimmed text starts with /', including Java-valid prefix inner comments that have code after the closing '/ token.
strip_inline_comment removes an ordinary apostrophe preceded by whitespace outside double quotes; this is broader than the Java TIM inner-comment iterator and changes some valid command semantics.
post_tim_seed_line and strip_inline_comment do not remove Java's /'''[-\w]*'''/ inner-comment form, so hidden-field and hidden-edge payloads remain visible and remain in the seed.

perturbations.evidence: Java emits PrefixKept from the prefix-comment line at data-source-line 3 and SuffixKept at line 4. Rust emits different gradient ids and swaps entity metadata/order, showing that the prefix/suffix inner-comment model is not Java-compatible.

Java removes hidden-field and hidden-edge from visible text and source identity, emitting gradient prefix g1t6lu6pqivr3p. Rust leaves both payloads visible, widens the diagram, and emits gradient prefix g1cjsdqxzi34i.

findings.finding: The account's inline-comment invariant is overbroad. Java's inspected TIM iterators do not implement Rust's whitespace-preceded trailing-apostrophe stripping. The quote_comment_axes held-out is valid Java and shows a skinparam line whose trailing apostrophe text is not a harmless identity-only comment in Java, while Rust strips it and changes shipped rendering.

The implementation does not model StringLocated#removeInnerComment prefix/suffix behavior. A Java-valid line beginning with /' ... '/ and continuing with real code survives in Java, but Rust's post_tim_seed_line treats any trimmed /' prefix as a removable comment line.

The implementation omits Java's /'''[-\w]*'''/ special inner-comment removal. Valid hidden payloads in member and edge labels remain visible in Rust and change both geometry and deterministic resource ids.

verdict_reason: Three fresh, unique, Java-valid perturbations over independent comment axes fail the prescribed no-oracle comparator. Per T14 held-out perturbation rules, the mechanism is rejected and the counterexamples remain preserved.
